claims.text: ISP: no client should be forced to depend on methods it does not use; when the code that calls or implements an interface needs different parts of it, split it into small, focused interfaces.
claims.source_hint: glossary entry isp; standard formulation in software design literature

claims.text: In C#, a non-abstract class implementing an interface must provide every interface method that has no default body (otherwise CS0535).
claims.source_hint: C# compiler error CS0535; C# interfaces docs

claims.text: If an interface method's parameters change, every class implementing that interface must change its implementation to keep compiling.
claims.source_hint: C# interfaces: implementing members must match the interface member signature

claims.text: IFullNotifier declares Send(int orderId, string subject), IReadOnlyList<string> History() and void Retry(int orderId); SmsOnlyNotifier implements it, prints in Send, and throws NotSupportedException from History ("this channel keeps no history") and Retry ("this channel does not retry").
INotifier declares exactly one member, void Send(int orderId, string subject); NotifierBase implements it and leaves abstract Format to EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier.
Code whose parameter or variable is typed IFullNotifier can only be given objects of classes that implement all three of its methods.
claims.source_hint: C# interfaces: implicit conversion only from classes implementing the interface

claims.text: A filler implementation that throws breaks substitutability: callers holding the interface may call that method and cannot know this implementation fails.
claims.source_hint: follows from LSP (previous lesson) and outline item 3

claims.text: Method count is a symptom; ISP is about whether each implementer and caller needs every method it is forced to depend on.
The comment above SmsOnlyNotifier (NotifierIspViolation.cs:14-15) names SmsNotifier, but the class it describes is SmsOnlyNotifier.
